### Supporting basis

Gzip level 6 offers a mature, universally supported algorithm with moderate compression ratios and consistent CPU usage. However, for repetitive JSON structures, it often struggles to maximize redundancy elimination compared to modern alternatives. Zstandard (Zstd) level 3 provides significantly higher decompression speeds, often exceeding 1 GB/s per core, which is crucial when archives are read repeatedly. While Zstd level 3 generally achieves better compression ratios than gzip level 6 for structured text data due to superior context modeling, its compression speed is roughly comparable or slightly faster. The key advantage of Zstd lies in its asymmetric capabilities; it excels in decompression throughput without sacrificing too much on compression time or ratio. Given the 10 GB dataset size and the specific use case of repeated reads, Zstd’s ability to quickly flush data to storage while enabling rapid subsequent reads makes it structurally superior. Gzip’s legacy support is largely irrelevant in modern environments where Zstd libraries are standard.

### Recommendation

I strongly recommend using Zstandard at compression level 3. This setting strikes an optimal balance between compression ratio and speed, specifically favoring the decompression throughput required for repeated reads. For 10 GB of newline-delimited JSON with repeated field names, Zstd leverages dictionary capabilities and better entropy coding to achieve smaller file sizes than gzip level 6, reducing storage costs. More importantly, its decompression speed is substantially higher, minimizing latency when multiple processes retrieve logs simultaneously. While gzip is a safe default, Zstd level 3 provides tangible performance benefits in both storage efficiency and read performance. The slight increase in implementation complexity is negligible in modern infrastructure. By choosing Zstd, you ensure faster archival creation times and significantly improved retrieval speeds, directly addressing the core constraints of high throughput and efficient repeated access. This choice aligns with industry trends toward Zstandard for log archiving, offering a superior practical performance profile for your specific workload.<|im_end|>
